record.paper_title: Control theory of stochastic distributed parameter systems: recent progress and open problems
record.context_brief: transposition solution for second adjoint equation
record.original_question: Let (3.7) denote the operator-valued backward stochastic evolution equation that currently has a unique relaxed transposition solution in the paper. Can one prove that this equation admits a unique transposition solution, not merely a relaxed transposition solution, in a substantially more general setting than the currently known very special case?

evidence.quote: If (3.7) admits a transposition solution, then it has a relaxed transposition solution ... Until now, we have no idea how to prove the existence of a transposition solution to (3.7).

(8) Well-posedness of (3.7) in the sense of transposition solution. It would be quite important for some optimal control problems to prove that equation (3.7) admits a unique transposition solution. So far this is only done for a very special case (e.g., [33, Theorem 4.1]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let $T>0$, let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\{\mathcal F_t\}_{t\in[0,T]},\mathbb P)$ be a complete filtered probability space on which a one-dimensional standard Brownian motion $\{W(t)\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ is defined and generates the filtration. Let $H$ be a separable Hilbert space and let $A:\mathcal D(A)\subset H\to H$ generate a $C_0$-semigroup on $H$. Denote by $\mathcal L(H)$ the space of bounded linear operators on $H$.

Consider, for given operator-valued data $J\in L^\infty_{\mathcal F_T}(\Omega;\mathcal L(H))$ (self-adjoint), $F\in L^1_{\mathbb F}(0,T;\mathcal L(H))$, $K_1,K_2,K_3\in L^2_{\mathbb F}(0,T;\mathcal L(H))$, the operator-valued backward stochastic evolution equation
$$\begin{cases} dP=-\bigl(A^*P+PA+K_1^*P+PK_1+K_2^*QK_3+K_3^*Q^*K_2+F\bigr)\,dt+Q\,dW(t),\quad t\in[0,T],\\ P(T)=J,\end{cases}\qquad (\star)$$
where the unknown is the pair of $\mathcal L(H)$-valued, $\mathbb F$-adapted processes $(P,Q)$. Such an equation arises as the second-order adjoint equation in Pontryagin-type maximum principles for stochastic evolution equations.

Notions of solution. A pair $(P,Q)$ is called a transposition solution of $(\star)$ if $P$ is a weakly measurable, essentially bounded, $\mathcal L(H)$-valued, $\mathbb F$-adapted process, $Q$ belongs to a suitable space of $\mathcal L(H)$-valued adapted processes, and a variational identity dual to $(\star)$ — tested against pairs of $H$-valued forward Itô processes — holds. A relaxed transposition solution replaces the single process $Q$ by a family of bilinear functionals $\{\hat Q^{(\cdot,\cdot)}\}$ chosen so that the analogous variational identity is satisfied for all admissible test processes. Every transposition solution induces a relaxed transposition solution, but the converse is not known in general. It is known that $(\star)$ admits a unique relaxed transposition solution under broad hypotheses, while existence and uniqueness of a (genuine) transposition solution has been established only in very restrictive special cases.

Problem. Identify a class of generators $A$, coefficients $(K_1,K_2,K_3,F)$, and terminal data $J$ that is substantially broader than the currently known special cases, and prove that within this class the operator-valued backward stochastic evolution equation $(\star)$ admits a unique transposition solution (not merely a unique relaxed transposition solution).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (e.g., a 2024 study on properties of transposition solutions to operator-valued BSEEs and applications to robust second-order necessary conditions) continue to develop the theory and applications of transposition/relaxed transposition solutions, but only relaxed transposition solutions are known in general; existence and uniqueness of a (non-relaxed) transposition solution to the second-order operator-valued adjoint equation is still established only in special cases. No general well-posedness result has appeared.

status_evidence.title: Properties for transposition solutions to operator-valued BSEEs, and applications to robust second order necessary conditions for controlled SEEs
status_evidence.snippet: Transposition method is adopted to deal with adjoint operator-valued backward stochastic evolution equations, especially correction terms.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies properties of transposition solutions to operator-valued BSEEs but does not establish general well-posedness in the transposition sense.

status_evidence.title: Operator-valued backward stochastic Lyapunov equations in infinite dimensions, and its application
status_evidence.snippet: Well-posedness ... in the sense of V-transposition solution and relaxed transposition solution.
status_evidence.claim: Existing well-posedness for related operator-valued BSEEs is in the relaxed/V-transposition sense, not the full transposition sense.
